html:
Union Minière du Haut Katanga (UMHK) was a Belgian mining company that ran the copper mines of Katanga in the Belgian Congo from 1906 to 1966. It was the economic heart of the colony.

It was set up in 1906 by Belgian financial groups and the British firm Tanganyika Concessions. Katanga sits on one of the world's richest copper belts, and the company also mined cobalt, zinc and other metals. It brought in African workers from across the region, at first in harsh conditions, and built towns, schools and hospitals for them under tight company control. Its copper went out by rail, later along the Benguela railway.

Its Shinkolobwe mine supplied much of the uranium for the American Manhattan Project in the Second World War.

When the Congo became independent in 1960, the company backed the breakaway State of Katanga under Moïse Tshombe. After the secession failed, Mobutu took over its Congo assets in 1966 and 1967 and created the state company Gécamines.
sum: Union Minière du Haut Katanga (UMHK) was a Belgian mining company that ran the copper mines of Katanga in the Belgian Congo from 1906 to 1966. It was the economic heart of the colony.
